title: TRY...CATCH
description: Learn how to handle exceptions gracefully using the TRY...CATCH construct.

data.text: The TRY...CATCH construct allows you to gracefully handle exceptions in SQL Server. Place statements that might cause an error in the TRY block and handle them in the CATCH block.

data.title: Basic TRY...CATCH syntax
data.code:
BEGIN TRY
    -- statements that may cause exceptions
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    -- statements that handle exception
END CATCH

items: ERROR_LINE() — returns the line number of the error.
ERROR_MESSAGE() — returns the complete error message text.
ERROR_PROCEDURE() — returns the name of the stored procedure or trigger.

data.text: Use XACT_STATE() in the CATCH block to check transaction state before committing or rolling back:

data.title: TRY...CATCH Key Points
points: TRY...CATCH provides structured error handling in T-SQL.
Use ERROR_* functions in the CATCH block to get error details.
Always check XACT_STATE() before committing or rolling back transactions.
